texts: mixed: the restriction to stored essence, the "stays" continuation and the "at least two years" reading of "for years" all survive, but the plain fact that the essence is good is recorded only inside the reified state, so a direct "is stored mire-essence good?" finds nothing. Giving the claim a countable bearer lets the plain property come along with the continuation: "Stored batches of mire-essence stay good for years."

bad: the parse asserts a single state of being good held by the kind itself and pitches it at "every"-strength rather than the strength a general claim gets, and once those unlicensed atoms come out there is nothing left to carry "stays" or "for six months" — the shelf life, which is the point of the sentence, is lost. Give the claim a countable bearer so the good-state has something to hold of and the six months has somewhere to attach: "Stored batches of mire-essence stay good for six months."
